about.title: Santa Paula Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a sudden collision reshapes everything, and the days that follow are rarely the time to also decode legal deadlines and paperwork. Santa Paula sits along SR-126 and other Ventura County corridors that carry steady local and pass-through traffic, and even where fatal outcomes are rare in the annual public record, a single loss changes a household for good. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents or heirs eligible if none of those relatives survive. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we simply listen to what happened, then connect your family with an independent attorney from our network who takes wrongful death matters on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. That first conversation costs nothing and creates no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file — spouses, domestic partners, and children have priority, with dependents or other heirs eligible in certain circumstances. An attorney can confirm who in your family qualifies before any filing decision is made.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death, Not the Crash
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved. Waiting to sort out paperwork can quietly cost your family that right.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help your family understand the fuller scope of what's recoverable.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to bring the claim. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. An independent attorney can review your family's specific relationships to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Santa Paula?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter if a government entity, such as a public road authority connected to SR-126 or another local corridor, is involved. It's worth having this reviewed early rather than assuming there's ample time.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as the police investigation or any criminal case?
items.answer: No — a wrongful death claim is a separate civil matter from any criminal charges that may or may not be filed. Even if no criminal case moves forward, your family may still have a valid civil claim. The two processes run independently and follow different rules and timelines.
